domain: Organizational Psychology / Systems Theory / Epistemology of Control
topic_summary: Analysis of a constraint topology realized in narrative form, depicting a Warden enforcing disposal protocols in an industrial vent system. The narrative demonstrates structural dynamics of measurement-dependent authority, protocol rigidity under temporal drift, and the collapse of observational fidelity when documentation requirements conflict with oscillating reality.

key_entities: Warden (enforcement agent operating via phrase-library and measurement protocols)
Phrase-library (fixed linguistic protocol mapping measurements to authorized responses)
Sync pulse (temporal calibration signal advancing irregularly)
Contamination readings (oscillating measurements at disposal threshold)
Upper administration queue (escalation sink with no assigned reader)
key_tensions: Protocol completeness vs unclassified phenomena (phrase-library has no entry for oscillation)
Measurement timing vs execution timing (reading changes between initiation and disposal)
Escalation architecture vs resolution capacity (reports route to originating domain)
key_mechanisms: Phrase-library protocol: measurement triggers phrase selection, phrase authorizes action, action generates log entry with single-field constraint
Temporal calibration drift: sync pulse advances consistently, no diagnostic branch resolves cause, escalation returns to sender
Oscillating threshold: contamination readings cross disposal threshold during phrase delivery, creating execution at sub-threshold state
absences: No protocol for mid-phrase correction or multi-state logging
No cross-domain resolution mechanism when escalation target is escalation source
